full_judgment: " This provision is almost similar to section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The intention of the legislature in inserting this provision and deletion of certain provisions is clear. The rights of the landlord of non-agricultural land which they had, even after the acquisition of rent receiving interest has been curtailed, on and from the date of promulgation of ordinance No. IX of 1967. There cannot be any new lease of non-agricultural land from the date of promulgation of the said ordinance. The expression "subletting" connotes the creation of a sub-ordinate tenancy or under raiyat, under which the sub-lessee would but for a special contract be liable to pay rent for that land to a person other than the Government. The purpose of inserting this section appears to be that since after the acquisition of the interest of rent receivers by the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the rent receivers were themselves to retain certain classes of retainable khas land as tenants directly under the Government, they should not be allowed to create further sub-tenancies under them. I am therefore, of the view that the plaintiffs status became tenants under th6 Government after section 26A, came into force. Considering this aspect of the matter, Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan finds difficult to oppose the rule. He however, feebly argues that the court of appeal below was justified in dismissing the suit.
